stanza: a cramped one-room home of a poor family in a remote mountain village, present day, late afternoon: plain painted walls with a few damp stains and nothing hanging on them except a small wooden crucifix; on the left an old black cast-iron wood stove, cold, with its small front door ajar and a folded white cloth stuffed inside instead of firewood; next to it a tiny kitchen corner with a chipped enamel sink and a two-burner gas cooker; on the right an unmade double bed with an iron headboard, a thin mattress and a crumpled brown blanket, and next to the bed a worn brown armchair with a small table beside it holding an old nebulizer machine; at the back a window with half-closed plastic roller blinds. A ceiling lamp gives even light.
persone: Two people face the viewer in tense silence. In the middle of the room stands a tired, hard-faced woman in her fifties with her arms crossed, in a shapeless dark grey cardigan over a faded housedress and worn slippers, her greying hair tied back carelessly: she has just woken up after a night shift. On the right, in the worn armchair next to the bed, sits her husband in his sixties, a heavy-boned, wasted former quarry worker with grey stubble and a shaved head, in an old vest under a brown wool blanket wrapped around his shoulders and legs, the plastic mask of the nebulizer hanging on his chest, struggling to breathe. They are hiding something, and their faces show it.
pose: the woman standing in the middle with her arms crossed and the man sitting in the armchair wrapped in the blanket
oggetti: the cold wood stove with its door ajar and the white cloth inside, the sink and the gas cooker, the unmade double bed, the armchair, the small table with the nebulizer, the window with the half-closed blinds and the crucifix
stranezze: The woman standing in the middle: healthy, clean and well fed, with smooth, even, slightly waxy skin and only a few soft wrinkles for her sixty years; but her face is wrong: her eyes are a little too big and set a little too far apart, perfectly round, with very dark irises and a fixed, unblinking stare; her nose is small and too straight; her mouth is slightly too wide, pressed in a thin straight line; her face is a little too long and too symmetrical; her grey hair is neat and stiff, almost like a wig. The man in the armchair: healthy-looking for his seventy years, not thin, with clean, smooth, pinkish skin and a clean-shaven, round, bald head; but he is wrong: his head is slightly too big and too round; his pale eyes are a little too far apart and do not seem to blink; his ears sit a little too low; his upper lip is unnaturally long; his slightly open mouth shows too many small, even, white teeth; his hands are a little too large, with fingers slightly too long. The plastic tube of the nebulizer still hangs on his chest.
